regions.text: 考へられる目所』について語り神にあつては「自由が無限である』と共に『實踐的必然性』があるといふ。

quote.translation: Boutroux speaks of "necessity in the form of duty", that is, of "the end conceived as necessary", and says that in God "freedom is infinite" whilst there is at the same time "practical necessity".

regions.text: また神の「不斷の攝理』「特殊の据理』を説き「宇宙のもろもうの形式や一般法則の段階組織が示す偶然性は、この神の自由の教説にょつて説明される』と云つてるる。

quote.translation: He expounds God's "unceasing providence" and "particular providence", and says that "the contingency shown by the hierarchical organisation of the various forms and general laws of the universe is explained by this doctrine of the freedom of God".

regions.text: きうして彼が櫻語として絶頭に揚げた『ここにもまた神々がある』といふアリストラレスの「動物の部分からの引用旬は、因果的偶然性の背後に溶む目前々必然性を指摘するものとして彼の立場を表明すると共に彼の思想が「ーマス・アクィナスの「必然性または偶然性の法則」の概念やマルブランシュの偶因諭と接近を有することを暗示してゐる。

quote.translation: The quotation from Aristotle's Parts of Animals that he placed at the head of his book as a motto, "Here too there are gods", indicates that his standpoint points to the teleological necessity lurking behind causal contingency, and at the same time hints that his thought is close to Thomas Aquinas's concept of the "law of necessity or of contingency" and to Malebranche's occasionalism.

regions.text: とを暗示してゐる。なほュミ、ール・ボレルもその著

quote.translation: Émile Borel, too, affirms causal contingency in his book Le Hasard.

regions.text: なほュミ、ール・ボレルもその著偶然において因果偶然を肯定してゐる。物理現象に開、する彼の主張によれば、一方において「或る一つの全體的現象の必然性は部分諸現象の自由と相容れないものではない』。他方に於て「部分的諸現象に関して絶對的と考へられた決定論も、絶對的嚴格を以て全蟹的現象を豫知することをば許さない』。

quote.translation: His claim concerning physical phenomena is, on the one hand, that "the necessity of a certain total phenomenon is not incompatible with the freedom of the partial phenomena", and, on the other, that "even a determinism thought to be absolute with regard to the partial phenomena does not permit the total phenomenon to be foreseen with absolute rigour".

regions.text: 絶對的な決定論はいごれにしても支持し難い。

quote.translation: Absolute determinism is in any case difficult to support.

regions.text: 「なせならば、宇宙内にあつて自由の干興するところが如何に小さくとも、さういふ干興の存

quote.translation: "For, however small the interference of freedom within the universe may be, between the universe in which such interference exists and the universe from which it is excluded an abyss lies" (Émile Borel, Le Hasard, 1920, pp. 290-295).
